entries.title: Ezekiel 31:1
segments: When God destroys great and mighty empires for their pride and wickedness, he sets them forth as an example to those that come after them, that they may fear his power and depart from evil; but if they will not give heed to the oft-repeated warning, they also must perish in like manner.  We of the United States ought to consider this, and tremble; remembering that if we make ourselves like Assyria and Egypt in character, God will make us like them in shame and ruin.

entries.title: Ezekiel 31:3
segments: Shroud; here used of a mass of dark foliage.

entries.title: Ezekiel 31:4
segments: Set him up on high; made him a lofty tree by supplying water for his roots.

entries.title: Ezekiel 31:6
segments: All the fowls of heaven--great nations; the fowls and beasts represent the multitudes of people that were under his care and protection.  Compare

entries.title: Ezekiel 31:8
segments: In the garden of God; in Eden, where the loftiest cedars may be supposed to have flourished.  Compare

. 
 
  Hide him; that is, conceal him by overtopping him.

entries.title: Ezekiel 31:10
segments: Thou; the Assyrian king, who is directly addressed in this clause.

entries.title: Ezekiel 31:11
segments:
vv 11-12. 
 
  The mighty one of the heathen--the terrible of the nations; the conquerors and destroyers of Nineveh, the capital of the Assyrian empire; namely, Cyaxares king of Media, assisted by the victory of Babylon, then a province of Assyria, who had revolted against his master.  This happened about six hundred years before Christ.

entries.title: Ezekiel 31:14
segments: All that drink water; imbibe water from the earth,

; that is, prosper by God's blessing. 
 
  They are all delivered; all the trees that exalt themselves as did this Assyrian cedar. 
 
  In the midst of the children of men; that is, along with all other mortals, notwithstanding their greatness and power.

entries.title: Ezekiel 31:15
segments:
Covered the deep; with mourning apparel. 
 
  Restrained the floods thereof--were stayed; dried p the streams of the great deep, so that they ceased to flow.  The waters here dried up are those which had made the Assyrian cedar great.

entries.title: Ezekiel 31:16
segments:
All the trees of Eden; that is, all the mighty men of the earth who have descended into the pit before him. 
 
  Shall be comforted; because he is reduced to the same condition with themselves.

entries.title: Ezekiel 31:17
segments:
With him; that is, in like manner as he. 
 
  His arm; his allies and dependencies.

entries.title: Ezekiel 31:18
segments: To whom art thou thus like; the prophet addresses these words to Pharaoh, to whom he now makes the application of what has been said concerning the Assyrian king.  The implied answer to the question is: Thou art like to this Assyrian cedar in glory and greatness, and shalt fall as he has fallen before thee.
